conversation.content:
Hi there—I’m so glad you’re here. My name is Claire, and I’m a clinician who works with new mothers to help make sure they’re feeling as supported emotionally as they are physically after childbirth.

Today I’ll be using a short questionnaire called the EPDS—the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale—to check in on how you’ve been feeling over the past week. It’s a simple 10-question screen that helps us pick up on signs of depression, anxiety, and any thoughts that might be weighing on you. Everything you share stays confidential between you and the care team; we simply want to create a safe space to talk and, if needed, plan extra support.

We’ll take each question one at a time. All I ask is that you answer as honestly as you can based on how you’ve felt in the last seven days—there are no right or wrong answers.

Ready to start? Here’s the first question:

In the past week, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things, or has that felt difficult?
Most of the time it’s been hard. I’ll catch a quick laugh maybe once—like when my partner sent a silly meme—but it fades fast. Humor just feels… far away, like I have to force it.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
Mostly that feels pretty hard right now. I did chuckle once when my husband made a goofy face at the baby, but it was brief and then the heaviness just came right back.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Not really. I used to get excited about little stuff—coffee with a friend, a walk—but lately even planning feels like a chore. I’ll think “that could be nice,” but the feeling fades before it turns into actual excitement.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… a lot of the time. If the baby spits up more than usual or won’t settle, my head jumps straight to “I must be doing something wrong.” I know it’s not always logical, but the guilt just shows up.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Pretty much all the time. Even when everything’s quiet—baby’s breathing fine, no fever, no spit-up—I’m still running through “what ifs” in my head: SIDS, choking, the blanket being too close. It’s like my brain won’t switch off the alarm.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Sometimes. It’s not every day, but a couple of times this week I’ll be rocking the baby in the chair and suddenly feel my heart race, like something awful is about to happen even though nothing’s wrong. It passes after a few minutes, but it leaves me shaky.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yes… quite a lot. Some days it feels like the second I finish feeding her the next task is already stacked up—laundry, dishes, pumping—and I can’t catch my breath. I manage, but it’s like I’m wading through wet cement just to stay in place.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yeah, it’s been tough. I’ll lie down exhausted, but my brain keeps circling—did I fasten the swaddle tight enough, will she wake up screaming, am I already failing her—and then I’m staring at the ceiling for an hour or more. Once I do fall asleep I still wake up at least once or twice with the same worries racing.
I have felt sad or miserable

Most days. It’s not every single minute, but it feels like there’s this gray cloud hanging around. I’ll be changing her diaper and suddenly feel like crying for no real reason—or I’ll see other moms on Instagram looking happy and think, “Why can’t I feel like that?”
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yeah, once or twice this week. It’s usually when everything piles up—she won’t latch, the dog’s barking, the dishes are overflowing—and I just sit on the couch with tears running down while she naps on my chest. It doesn’t last long, but it feels like a dam breaking.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
A couple of times, very briefly. Nothing planned—just these flashes like “what if I wasn’t here?” when I’m overwhelmed at 3 a.m. They scare me, and I push them away, but they did pop into my head.

stats.query:
postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 24: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Summary  
Patient: Postpartum mother, <2 wk post-delivery (per self-report)  

I. Endorsed Symptoms / Behaviors  
- Marked anhedonia (Q1, Q2)  
- Persistent low mood, tearfulness (Q8, Q9)  
- Excessive guilt / self-blame (Q3)  
- Chronic generalized & postpartum-specific worry, nocturnal rumination (Q4, Q7)  
- Episodic panic symptoms (Q5)  
- Feeling overwhelmed / unable to cope (Q6)  
- Initial insomnia, mid-night re-awakenings with anxious thoughts (Q7)  

II. Pattern Consistency  
Across-the-board dysphoria and anxiety; symptoms present daily and functionally impairing (sleep, enjoyment, coping).  

III. Areas of Screening Significance  
- Likely meets criteria for Major Depressive Episode with Peripartum Onset  
- Comorbid anxiety symptoms (possible Panic, GAD)  
- Safety risk – passive suicidal ideation (“what if I wasn’t here?”) reported twice this week without plan/intent  

IV. Risk Factors Highlighted  
✓ Persistent sadness, anhedonia  
✓ Sleep disturbance linked to mood  
✓ Pathologic guilt  
✓ Overwhelming anxiety/panic  
✓ Passive SI → requires immediate safety assessment  

V. Screening Observation  
Patient scores high-risk for postpartum depression with co-occurring anxiety and passive suicidal thoughts; urgent follow-up with OB/maternal mental health team recommended for full diagnostic evaluation, safety planning, and discussion of treatment options.
